The Railroad Retirement Board (RRB) is directed by
45 U.S.C. 231f(c)(2)
to establish a financial interchange (FI) between the railroad retirement and social security systems to place the Social Security Old-Age and Survivors Insurance (OASI) and Disability Insurance (DI) Trust Funds and the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Hospital Insurance (HI) Trust Fund in the same condition they would have been had railroad employment been covered by the Social Security Act and Federal Insurance Contributions Act (FICA). Each year, the RRB estimates the benefits and expenses that would have been paid by these trust funds, as well as the payroll taxes and income taxes that would have been received by them. To make these estimates, the RRB requires information on all earnings data that are not taxable under the Railroad Retirement Tax Act (RRTA) but would be taxable under FICA.
The payroll information collected from the BA-15 is essential for the calculation of payroll taxes and benefits used by the FI. Failure to collect NQSOs and ratification payment information will result in understating the payroll taxes that should have been collected and the benefit amounts that would have been payable under the Social Security Act for FI purposes. Accurate compensation file tabulations are also an integral part of the data needed to estimate future tax revenues and corresponding FI amounts. Without information on NQSOs and ratification payments, the amount of funds to be transferred between the RRB, SSA and CMS cannot be determined.
Form BA-15, Report of Stock Options and Other Payments, to request employer information and report identifying information as well as each employee's social security number, name, and compensation information, which will be reported annually in a quarterly breakdown. The RRB receives Form BA-15 by secure Email, File Transfer Protocol (FTP), or via CD-ROM. The RRB proposes no changes to Form BA-15.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34—106732; File No. SR-IEX-2026-42]
October 26, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1)
[
1
]
of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”)
[
2
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
3
]
notice is hereby given that, on October 15, 2026, the Investors Exchange LLC (“IEX” or the “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II and III below, which Items have been prepared by the self-regulatory organization. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
Pursuant to the provisions of Section 19(b)(1) under the Act,
[
4
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
5
]
the Exchange is filing with the Commission a proposed rule change to modify the behavior of Discretionary Peg orders if they are received by the Exchange during a period of quote instability or quote imbalance. The Exchange has designated this rule filing as non-controversial under Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
6
]
and paragraph (f)(6) of Rule 19b-4 thereunder.
[
7
]
The text of the proposed rule change is available at the Exchange's website at
https://www.iexexchange.io/​resources/​regulation/​rule-filings
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and the Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the self-regulatory organization included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received
(
printed page 68202)
on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The self-regulatory organization has prepared summaries, set forth in Sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and the Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The purpose of this proposed rule filing is to amend Rule 11.190(b)(10) with respect to Discretionary Peg (“D-Peg”) orders, so that a D-Peg order received during a period of quote instability
[
8
]
or quote imbalance,
[
9
]
as selected by the User
[
10
]
for that order, initially prices and posts at its resting price
[
11
]
rather than first pricing at the less aggressive of the Midpoint Price
[
12
]
or the order's limit price, if any. IEX also proposes to make conforming edits to Rules 11.190(a)(3), 11.190(h)(3)(C)(ii), and 11.190(h)(3)(D)(ii). This proposal will only apply to D-Peg orders with a time-in-force (“TIF”)
[
13
]
that allows the D-Peg to post to the Order Book.
Background
Currently, upon entry into the System,
[
14
]
a D-Peg order seeks to execute against orders resting on the Order Book at the least aggressive of the Midpoint Price or the order's limit price, if any. If the D-Peg order has a TIF of IOC
[
15
]
or FOK,
[
16
]
any unexecuted shares are canceled back to the User. If the D-Peg order has a TIF of DAY,
[
17
]
GTX,
[
18
]
SYS,
[
19
]
or GTT
[
20
]
(collectively referred to herein as a “bookable D-Peg order”), any unexecuted shares post to the Order Book at the less aggressive of one minimum price variant (“MPV”)
[
21
]
less aggressive than the primary quote (the NBB for a buy order or the NBO for a sell order) or the order's limit price, if any.
[
22
]
A resting D-Peg order will exercise the least amount of price discretion necessary to meet the limit price of an active contra-side order, up to its discretionary price.
[
23
]
However, during a period of quote instability or quote imbalance, as applicable, the D-Peg order will not exercise any discretion and is only eligible to trade at its resting price.
[
24
]
Quote instability determinations are made by the System using the “crumbling quote indicator” or “CQI”,
[
25
]
and periods of quote imbalance are determined by the System using the “quote imbalance indicator” or “QII”.
[
26
]
Users designate whether the CQI or QII should apply to each D-Peg order, which means each resting D-Peg order's discretion will always be restricted either during times of quote instability or quote imbalance, as specified by the User,
[
27
]
while an incoming D-Peg order currently is unaffected by whether it is received during a period of quote instability or quote imbalance, as described above.
Proposal
The Exchange proposes to extend the CQI and QII protections to incoming bookable D-Peg orders that arrive while the applicable quote instability or quote imbalance determination is in effect for its side of the market.
As proposed, an incoming bookable D-Peg order will not seek to execute against orders resting on the Order Book at the least aggressive of the Midpoint Price or the order's limit price, if any, if it arrives during a period of quote instability or quote imbalance, as applicable. Instead, under this proposal, such a D-Peg order will post to the Order Book at either the less aggressive of one MPV less aggressive than the primary quote, or the order's limit price, if any. When on entry the CQI or QII, as applicable, is not in effect, a bookable D-Peg order will, as is currently the case, seek to execute against orders resting on the Order Book at the least aggressive of the Midpoint Price or the order's limit price, if any, and any unexecuted shares will post to the Order Book at either the less aggressive of one MPV less aggressive than the primary quote, or the order's limit price, if any. The Exchange is not proposing any change to the behavior of non-bookable D-Peg orders (
i.e.,
orders with a TIF of IOC or FOK), which will continue to seek to execute against orders resting on the Order Book at the least aggressive of the Midpoint Price or the order's limit price, if any, irrespective of if they arrive during a period of quote instability or quote imbalance, as applicable.
This proposal also changes nothing about the behavior of resting D-Peg orders, which will continue to exercise the least amount of price discretion necessary to meet the limit price of an active contra-side order, up to the D-Peg order's discretionary price, when the CQI or QII, as applicable, is not in effect. However, during a period of quote instability or quote imbalance, as applicable, resting D-Peg orders will continue to not exercise any price discretion, meaning they remain eligible to trade only at their resting price.
[
28
]
The following examples depict how this proposed change will impact incoming D-Peg orders:
Example 1 (existing functionality)
Market for security ABC is $10.10 by $10.12.
IEX has a resting M-Peg
[
29
]
to sell 100 shares, which is booked at the Midpoint Price of $10.11.
CQI determines the Signal Best Bid
[
30
]
is unstable.
IEX receives a D-Peg order to buy 100 shares with limit of $10.11, TIF of DAY, and User designation that the D-Peg should apply the CQI.
D-Peg order is automatically priced at $10.11 and takes the resting M-Peg, irrespective of the quote being unstable.
Example 2 (proposed functionality)
Market for security ABC is $10.10 by $10.12.
IEX has a resting M-Peg
[
31
]
to sell 100 shares, which is booked at the Midpoint Price of $10.11.
CQI determines the Signal Best Bid is unstable.
IEX receives a D-Peg order to buy 100 shares with limit of $10.11, TIF of DAY, and User designation that the D-Peg should apply the CQI.
D-Peg order is automatically priced at $10.09 and does not trade with the resting M-Peg.
This proposal merely aligns the entry pricing of a bookable D-Peg order with the order's existing restriction on exercising price discretion during a period of quote instability or quote imbalance, as applicable. The proposed change is confined to this entry-pricing circumstance for bookable D-Peg orders. It does not change how the Exchange calculates quote instability or quote
(
printed page 68203)
imbalance, the resting price formula, or the order's discretionary price when the selected determination is not in effect.
Finally, the Exchange proposes two conforming changes to Rule 11.190(h)(3)
[
32
]
to clarify that a bookable D-Peg order will not execute on entry in a locked or crossed market if the CQI or QII, as applicable, is in effect. Under current rules, incoming bookable D-Peg orders could execute on entry in a locked or crossed market regardless of the CQI or QII state.
To implement the change, the Exchange proposes to revise the introductory text of Rule 11.190(b)(10), as well as references to D-Peg pricing on entry in Rules 11.190(a)(3), 11.190(h)(3)(C)(ii), and 11.190(h)(3)(D)(ii). Specifically, IEX proposes to make the following changes:
In the explanatory paragraph in Rule 11.190(b)(10), insert a new sentence after the sentence that reads: “A pegged order that upon entry into the System, the price of the order is automatically adjusted by the System to be equal to the less aggressive of the Midpoint Price or the order's limit price, if any.” The new sentence will read in full:
“However, if the order is submitted with a TIF of DAY, GTX, SYS, or GTT, and is received during a period of quote instability as defined in paragraph (g)(1) or a period of quote imbalance as defined in paragraph (g)(2) below, as selected by the User, the price of the order is automatically adjusted by the System to be equal to and ranked at the less aggressive of one (1) MPV less aggressive than the primary quote (
i.e.,
the NBB for buy orders and NBO for sell orders) or the order's limit price, if any, and posts to the Order Book.”
In the explanatory paragraph in Rule 11.190(a)(3) (Pegged Order), in the section describing D-Peg order pricing, add the following language after the words “the midpoint of the NBBO upon entry”:
“(except during periods of quote instability as defined in paragraph (g)(1) or during periods of quote imbalance as defined in paragraph (g)(2) below, as selected by the User), one (1) MPV less aggressive than the primary quote (
i.e.,
the NBB for buy orders and NBO for sell orders)”
IEX also proposes to remove the words “the inside quote on the same side of the market” that currently follow the proposed new text in Rule 11.190(a)(3), to address an inconsistency in Rule 11.190(a)(3)'s description of D-Peg's resting price.
[
33
]
In Rule 11.190(h)(3)(C)(ii), which describes D-Peg price sliding in the event that the market becomes locked, add the following text to the last sentence, after it describes how a D-Peg order tries to execute at the Midpoint Price if it is submitted while the market is locked:
“unless the order is submitted with a TIF of DAY, GTX, SYS, or GTT, and is received during a period of quote instability as defined in paragraph (g)(1) or a period of quote imbalance as defined in paragraph (g)(2) below, as selected by the User.”
In Rule 11.190(h)(3)(D)(ii), which describes D-Peg and P-Peg
[
34
]
price sliding in the event that the market becomes crossed, add the following text to the second sentence, after it describes how a D-Peg order tries to execute at the crossing price if it is submitted while the market is crossed:
“unless the order is submitted with a TIF of DAY, GTX, SYS, or GTT, and is received during a period of quote instability as defined in paragraph (g)(1) or a period of quote imbalance as defined in paragraph (g)(2) below, as selected by the User.”
Implementation
The Exchange will announce the implementation date of the proposed rule change by Trading Alert at least ten days in advance of such implementation date and within 90 days of effectiveness of this proposed rule change.
2. Statutory Basis
IEX believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the provisions of Section 6(b)
[
35
]
of the Act in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act
[
36
]
in particular, in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest because it is designed to protect from adverse selection bookable D-Peg orders that arrive during periods of quote instability or quote imbalance, by limiting execution at the Midpoint Price when the Exchange's CQI or QII, as applicable, identifies that the primary quote appears to be moving adversely to them, thereby reducing the potential to execute at an imminently stale price and enhancing the overall execution experience of D-Peg orders.
In addition, the Exchange believes that the proposed rule change will make D-Peg order handling more consistent and predictable, by extending the protection from execution at a potentially imminently stale price to bookable D-Peg orders on entry. Under the existing rule, an incoming D-Peg order received during a period of quote instability or quote imbalance, as applicable, is eligible to execute against resting interest up to the Midpoint Price on entry (unless constrained by the order's limit price), even though a resting D-Peg order is restricted from exercising price discretion to the Midpoint Price during such times.
Further, the Exchange believes that such protection is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest because it may incentivize the entry of additional D-Peg orders on the Exchange, thereby increasing the overall liquidity profile on the Exchange to the benefit of all market participants. Moreover, resting D-Peg orders generally provide liquidity to market participants removing liquidity on the Exchange when the CQI or QII, as applicable, is not in effect. By incentivizing the entry of additional D-Peg orders, the Exchange believes that the proposed changes may enhance the overall execution experience for other market participants removing liquidity on the Exchange when the CQI or QII, as applicable, is not in effect.
Furthermore, as noted in the Purpose section, the proposed pricing for a bookable D-Peg order that arrives during a period of quote instability or quote imbalance, as applicable, is the same as the pricing that occurs if any incoming bookable D-Peg order does not fully execute on entry. Thus, IEX does not believe that the proposed changes raise any new or novel issues that have not already been considered by the Commission in connection with existing order types and functionality offered by the Exchange.
Additionally, IEX believes that updating the descriptions of how orders are repriced in the Pegged Order rule, as well as in the rules for handling incoming D-Peg orders when the market is locked or crossed, is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest because it is designed to reduce the potential to execute at an imminently stale price and thereby enhance the overall execution experience of D-Peg orders.
Finally, the Exchange believes that the conforming change to the description of the resting price of D-Peg orders in the Pegged Orders rule is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest because it adds additional clarity to the Exchange's rules, thereby making them more accurate and complete, and
(
printed page 68204)
descriptive of the System's functionality.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
IEX does not believe that the proposed rule change will result in any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
The Exchange does not believe the proposal would impose an unnecessary or undue burden on intermarket competition. Market participants may choose among competing venues and order types. The proposal refines the handling of an existing IEX order type in a limited set of circumstances, in a manner designed to reduce the potential to execute at an imminently stale price and thereby enhance the overall execution experience of D-Peg orders which may help the Exchange compete with other exchanges for order flow. This order handling change will be available to all Members
[
37
]
on equal terms. Further, market participants have a variety of order types to select from (on IEX as well as on other equities exchanges) and have the ability to choose among these various order types to meet their specific trading or business needs, as determined by the Members. Accordingly, the Exchange believes that the proposed rule change will not result in any burden on intermarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
The Exchange also does not believe the proposal would impose an unnecessary or undue burden on intramarket competition. The proposed change will modify the treatment of all bookable D-Peg orders that are received by the Exchange during a period of quote instability or quote imbalance, as applicable, and will therefore be applied equally to all Members using the D-Peg order type, and the proposal does not alter the treatment of other order types.
Moreover, as discussed in the Statutory Basis sections, resting D-Peg orders generally provide liquidity to market participants removing liquidity on the Exchange. Thus, the Exchange further believes that to the extent that the proposed changes incentivize additional D-Peg order flow, for the reasons discussed in the Statutory Basis section, the proposed order handling change will enhance competition in a manner that is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
Written comments were neither solicited nor received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The Exchange has designated this rule filing as non-controversial under Section 19(b)(3)(A)
[
38
]
of the Act and Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
39
]
thereunder. Because the proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change meets the criteria of subparagraph (f)(6) of Rule 19b-4
[
40
]
because it would not significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest because it merely extends a bookable D-Peg order's existing restriction on discretionary pricing during periods of quote instability or quote imbalance, as applicable, to the order's initial pricing on entry. The rule change proposal does not alter the CQI or QII calculations, the order's resting price, or its ability to exercise discretion outside of periods of quote instability or quote imbalance, as applicable. Further, as discussed in the Burden on Competition section, above, this proposal would not impose any significant burden on competition. Furthermore, Rule 19b-4(f)(6) requires a self-regulatory organization to give the Commission written notice of its intent to file the proposed rule change at least five business days prior to the date of filing of the proposed rule change, or such shorter time as designated by the Commission. The Exchange has satisfied this requirement.
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings under Section 19(b)(2)(B)
[
41
]
of the Act to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-IEX-2026-42 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-IEX-2026-42. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-IEX-2026-42 and should be submitted on or before November 19, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
42
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

[Release No. 34-106739; File No. SR-CBOE-2026-082]
(
printed page 68205)
October 26, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 15, 2026, Cboe Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “Cboe Options”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
Cboe Exchange, Inc. (“Cboe” or the “Exchange”) is filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission” or “SEC”) a proposed rule change to remove the Silexx fees from its Fee Schedule in accordance with SEC exemptive relief issued on May 1, 2026. The text of the proposed rule change is provided in Exhibit 5.
The text of the proposed rule change is also available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
), the Exchange's website (
https://www.cboe.com/​us/​options/​regulation/​rule_​filings/​cone/​
), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to remove the Silexx Fee Schedule in its entirety pursuant to exemptive relief granted from the Commission.
[
3
]
By way of background, the Exchange's affiliate, Cboe Silexx, LLC, offers Silexx (an order entry management system or “OEMS”). Silexx is deemed a “facility” of the Exchange as that term is defined in Section 3(a)(2) of the Exchange Act.
[
4
]
Silexx allows authorized Users with direct access to the Exchange to establish connectivity and submit orders directly to the Exchange. Silexx Users may also send orders to other exchanges and are not required to send orders to the Exchange in order to use Silexx. Furthermore, TPHs are not required to use Silexx in order to access the Exchange; TPHs may also use an OEMS supported by a third-party to enter and route orders for execution to the Exchange and manage such executions.
As a facility of the Exchange, Silexx must satisfy the regulatory requirements applicable to a national securities exchange, including certain rule filing requirements under Section 19(b) and the requirements under Section 6(b) of the Exchange Act.
[
5
]
In compliance with these requirements, the Exchange has filed numerous proposed rule changes on behalf of Silexx.
[
6
]
On May 1, 2026, the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission” or the “SEC”) granted conditional exemptive relief pursuant to its authority under Section 36(a)(1) of the Exchange Act
[
7
]
to the Exchange for Exchange-Affiliated OEMSs (including Silexx) from the rule filing requirements under Section 19(b) of the Exchange Act and the requirements under Section 6(b) of the Exchange Act (the “Exemptive Relief”).
[
8
]
Meaning, that so long as the Exchange meets the conditions set out in the Exemptive Relief with respect to an Exchange-Affiliated OEMS, including Silexx, the Exchange (i) need not abide by the rule filing requirements under the Exemptive Relief pursuant to Section 19(b) and (ii) is not required to operate in accordance with Section 6(b) of the Exchange Act with respect to that Exchange-Affiliated OEMS, such as the requirement that fees are not unfairly discriminatory (under 6(b)(4)) or that fees do not impose an undue burden on competition (under 6(b)(8)).
In particular, the Exemptive Relief specifies that the following conditions must be met with respect to an Exchange-Affiliated OEMS, including Silexx, in order for the Exchange to benefit from this relief:
(i) The use of the Exchange-Affiliated OEMS is voluntary (
i.e.,
solely within the discretion of an Exchange member or other user of the OEMS) and not required for an Exchange member to access the Exchange.
(ii) There will be no differences between how third-party and Exchange-Affiliated OEMSs may connect to the Exchange.
(iii) The Exchange-Affiliated OEMS (or the entity that owns the Exchange-Affiliated OEMS) is not a registered broker-dealer.
(iv) For any order ultimately routed to the Exchange via an Exchange-Affiliated OEMS, the users of such OEMS and their brokers are solely responsible for routing decisions (
i.e.,
the Exchange is not involved in such routing decisions). All orders received by the Exchange from a third-party or Exchange-Affiliated OEMS shall be processed by the Exchange in the same manner and pursuant to the Exchange's rules.
(v) Any fees charged by the Exchange-Affiliated OEMS to a user thereof must not take into consideration any of that user's Exchange activity or Exchange fees set forth on the Exchange's fee schedule.
(vi) Users of third-party OEMSs and Exchange-Affiliated OEMSs will have use of the Exchange facilities and services (
e.g.,
Exchange market data) in the same manner pursuant to the same terms, conditions, and fees as set forth
(
printed page 68206)
in the Exchange's Rules, technical specifications, and Fees Schedule.
(vii) The Exchange has established and maintains procedures and internal controls reasonably designed to prevent the Exchange-Affiliated OEMS from receiving any advantage or benefit as a result of its affiliation/relationship with the Exchange, including the provision of Exchange information to the entity or personnel operating the Exchange-Affiliated OEMS regarding updates to the Exchange trading system (such as technical specifications) until such information is available generally to similarly situated market participants.
Importantly, in compliance with the terms of the Exemptive Relief, the Exchange has established and maintains procedures and internal controls reasonably designed to ensure compliance with the terms of the Exemptive Relief. Based on the Exemptive Relief, with respect to Exchange-Affiliated OEMSs, including Silexx, the Exchange is no longer required to undergo the rule filing process and is not required to operate in accordance with Section 6(b) obligations which, among other items, requires that fees are not unfairly discriminatory and, as such, the Exchange may consider having different pricing for its customers.
Accordingly, the Exchange proposes to remove the Silexx Fee Schedule in its entirety. Going forward, fees will be established as part of a contract, as opposed to residing within the Exchange's Fee Schedule. To avoid confusion between having pricing within a customer's contract and potentially differing prices within the Silexx Fee Schedule, the Exchange proposes to remove this Fee Schedule from its website and notes that these fees are no longer applicable—instead, customers will be bound by the fees within their contracts.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange. Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Exemptive Relief granted by the Commission with respect to Exchange-Affiliated OEMSs, including Silexx. The purpose of this filing is to implement the Exemptive Relief. With respect to Exchange-Affiliated OEMSs, including Silexx, the Exchange is not required to comply with Section 6(b) obligations, such as the Section 6(b)(5)
[
9
]
requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers, as well as Section 6(b)(4)
[
10
]
as it is designed to provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its Members and other persons using its facilities.
By removing Silexx fees from its Fee Schedule, the Exchange provides clarity for Silexx Users as they will be bound by the pricing within their contract, as opposed to an online fee schedule. As such, removing potentially conflicting fees prevents confusion between stale online fees and fees within a contract. This is consistent with the Exemptive Relief, which permits fees charged by an Exchange-Affiliated OEMS to be competitively established and to vary among users of such Exchange-Affiliated OEMS.
While the Exchange may consider charging Silexx Users different fees, this is in compliance with its Exemptive Relief. In the Exemptive Relief, the Commission explicitly notes that, “fees charged by an Exchange-Affiliated OEMS may be competitively established and may vary among users of such Exchange-Affiliated OEMS.”
[
11
]
While pricing may vary between Silexx Users, this is permitted under the Exemptive Relief received.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The Exchange does not believe the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intramarket and intermarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The purpose of this filing is to implement the Exemptive Relief with respect to Exchange-Affiliated OEMSs, including Silexx. The Exchange's removal of the Silexx fees from the Silexx Fee Schedule is consistent with the Exemptive Relief granted by the Commission, which permits fees charged by an Exchange-Affiliated OEMS to be established competitively and vary among users.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange neither solicited nor received comments on the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
12
]
and paragraph (f) of Rule 19b-4
[
13
]
thereunder. At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission will institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-CBOE-2026-082 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-CBOE-2026-082. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-CBOE-2026-082 and should be submitted on or before November 19, 2026.
(
printed page 68207)
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
14
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

notice is hereby given that, on October 15, 2026, NYSE American LLC (“NYSE American” or the “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the self-regulatory organization. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend the NYSE American Options Fee Schedule (“Fee Schedule”) to modify pricing for the Customer Best Execution (“CUBE”) Auctions. The Exchange proposes to implement the fee change effective October 15, 2026. The proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
www.nyse.com
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the self-regulatory organization included statements concerning the purpose of, and basis for, the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of those statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and the Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The purpose of this filing is to amend the Fee Schedule to modify participant rebates offered for initiating CUBE Auctions.
[
4
]
The Exchange proposes to implement the fee change effective October 15, 2026.
[
5
]
Background
The Exchange has established various pricing incentives designed to encourage increased electronic volume executed on the Exchange, including, but not limited to, the American Customer Engagement (“ACE”) Program.
[
6
]
To encourage participation in the ACE Program and CUBE Auctions, the Exchange offers an ACE Initiating Participant Rebate to ACE Program participants that initiate Single-Leg CUBE Auctions,
[
7
]
Complex CUBE Auctions,
[
8
]
and AON Single-Leg or AON Complex CUBE Auctions.
[
9
]
Currently, the ACE Initiating Participant Rebate for each of these auctions $0.12 per contact for all issues (
i.e.,
penny and non-penny).
In addition, the Exchange offers the Alternative Initiating Participant Rebate that enables non-ACE Program participants to qualify for this Rebate on certain initiating Complex CUBE
(
printed page 68197)
Auctions provided they meet certain monthly volume qualification levels and increase their initiating CUBE volume.
[
10
]
Currently, the Alternative Initiating Participant Rebate is $0.12 per contract for all issues.
Another incentive program offered by the Exchange is the Professional Volume Incentive Program under which ATP Holders that achieve Electronic volume in the Professional Customer, Broker Dealer, Non-NYSE American Options Market Maker, and Firm range (
i.e.,
the “Professional Range”) are eligible to receive discounted rates on their total monthly Professional Volume and credits on their monthly Customer Electronic volume.
[
11
]
To encourage participation in this program and CUBE Auctions, the Exchange offers a Professional Volume Incentive Initiating Participant Rebate to program participants that initiate Single-Leg CUBE Auctions, Complex CUBE Auctions, or AON Single-Leg or AON Complex CUBE Auctions.
[
12
]
Currently, the Professional Volume Incentive Initiating Participant Rebate for each of these auctions $0.12 per contact for all issues (
i.e.,
penny and non-penny).
Proposal
The Exchange proposes to reduce the ACE Initiating Participant Rebate for all three auctions and the Alternative Initiating Participant Rebate, for Complex CUBE Auctions, from $0.12 per contract to $0.115 per contract across all issues. The proposed change is the result of the Exchange's ongoing reassessment and rebalancing of its fee structure overall and, in this instance, its CUBE rebate structure. The proposal slightly reduces the amount of the ACE Initiating Participant Rebate and the Alternative Initiating Participant Rebate where applicable. As such, the Exchange believes that the Rebates will continue to encourage ATP Holders to initiate CUBE Auctions, whether single-leg, complex, or AON. Accordingly, the Exchange believes all market participants stand to benefit from the continuing increased order flow, which promotes market depth, facilitates tighter spreads and enhances price discovery. Increased order flow promotes market depth, facilitates tighter spreads and enhances price discovery, which enhances market quality for all participants.
The Exchange also proposes to eliminate the Professional Volume Incentive Initiating Participant Rebate program for Single-leg CUBE Auctions, Complex CUBE Auctions and AON Single-Leg/AON Complex CUBE Auctions. The Exchange adopted this rebate program in an effort to attract greater liquidity to the Exchange generally and believed, therefore, that it would benefit all market participants increased order flow, which promotes market depth, facilitates tighter spreads and enhances price discovery. It was hoped that this increased order flow would improve price discovery and make the Exchange a more competitive venue for order execution, which, in turn, would improve market quality for all market participants. However, the Rebate has been underutilized and thus has not achieved its intended effect. As a result, the Exchange now proposes to eliminate it from the Fee Schedule.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
13
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Sections 6(b)(4) and (5) of the Act,
[
14
]
in particular, because it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its members, issuers and other persons using its facilities and does not unfairly discriminate between customers, issuers, brokers or dealers.
As a threshold matter, the Exchange is subject to significant competitive forces in the market for options securities transaction services that constrain its pricing determinations in that market. The Commission has repeatedly expressed its preference for competition over regulatory intervention in determining prices, products, and services in the securities markets. In Regulation NMS, the Commission highlighted the importance of market forces in determining prices and SRO revenues and, also, recognized that current regulation of the market system “has been remarkably successful in promoting market competition in its broader forms that are most important to investors and listed companies.”
[
15
]
There are currently 20 registered options exchanges competing for order flow. Based on publicly available information and, excluding index-based options, no single exchange has more than 16% of the market share of executed volume of multiply-listed equity and ETF options trades.
[
16
]
Therefore, currently no exchange possesses significant pricing power in the execution of multiply-listed equity and ETF options order flow. More specifically, in August 2026, the Exchange had 11.30% market share of executed volume of multiply-listed equity and ETF options order flow. In such a low concentrated and highly competitive market, no single options exchange possesses significant pricing power in the execution of option order flow.
In response to these competitive forces and as discussed herein, the Exchange has established various pricing incentives regarding its CUBE Auctions, including, but not limited to, the ACE Initiating Participant Rebate, the Alternative Initiating Rebate and Professional Volume Incentive Initiating Participant Rebate, which are designed to encourage ATP Holders to utilize the CUBE Auction and to direct (increased) volume to the Exchange.
The Exchange believes that the proposed change in ACE Initiating Participant Rebate and the Alternative Initiating Rebates is reasonable, equitable, and not unfairly discriminatory and will continue to provide the intended incentive for ATP Holders to utilize the CUBE Auctions. To the extent this purpose is achieved, the Exchange believes that the proposed rebate reduction would not discourage ATP Holders from directing activity to the Exchange. The Exchange also believes that the proposal represents an equitable allocation of credits and is not unfairly discriminatory because the proposal will apply equally to all similarly situated ATP Holders.
Additionally, the Exchange believes that the elimination of the Professional Volume Incentive Initiating Participant Rebate for Single-leg CUBE Auctions, Complex CUBE Auctions and AON Single-Leg/AON Complex CUBE Auctions is reasonable, equitable, and
(
printed page 68198)
not unfairly discriminatory. Its removal would affect all similarly situated ATP Holders equally. Moreover, the program has not encouraged participants in the Professional Range to increase their participation in CUBE Auctions and eliminating this underutilized incentive program would simplify the Fee Schedule.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
In accordance with Section 6(b)(8) of the Act, the Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change would impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
Intramarket Competition.
The Exchange believes that the proposed change to the ACE Initiating Participant Rebate and the Alternative Initiating Rebates would not affect intramarket competition because, as noted above, it would impact all market participants equally and, therefore, would not impose a disparate burden on competition among market participants on the Exchange. Similarly, the proposed change is designed to continue to attract order flow to the Exchange by offering ATP Holders competitive incentives to continue to direct their order flow to the Exchange, thereby increasing liquidity to the benefit of all market participants.
In addition, the Exchange believes that the proposed elimination of the Professional Volume Incentive Initiating Participant Rebate would not affect intramarket competition because, as noted above, the program has not effectively encouraged increased professional range participation, and its elimination would impact all similarly situated ATP Holders equally.
Intermarket Competition.
The Exchange believes that the proposed change to the ACE Initiating Participant Rebate and the Alternative Initiating Rebates would not affect intermarket competition. As noted above, the Exchange operates in a highly competitive market in which the Exchange must continually adjust its fees and rebates to remain competitive with other exchanges and to attract order flow to the Exchange. The proposed change reflects this competitive reality.
In addition, the Exchange believes that the proposed elimination of the Professional Volume Incentive Initiating Participant Rebate for Single-leg CUBE Auctions, Complex CUBE Auctions and AON Single-Leg/AON Complex CUBE Auctions would not affect intramarket competition because, as noted above, the programs have not effectively encouraged increased Floor Broker participation, and its elimination would impact all Floor Brokers equally.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were solicited or received with respect to the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change is effective upon filing pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)
[
17
]
of the Act and subparagraph (f)(2) of Rule 19b-4
[
18
]
thereunder, because it establishes a due, fee, or other charge imposed by the Exchange.
At any time within 60 days of the filing of such proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings under Section 19(b)(2)(B)
[
19
]
of the Act to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-NYSEAMER-2026-94 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-NYSEAMER-2026-94. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-NYSEAMER-2026-94 and should be submitted on or before November 19, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
20
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.
